subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Pantograph: Scaling Motion
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Pantograph: Scaling Motion usable.

hook.text: Trace a small drawing and a larger copy appears. A linkage scales it.

buildup.text: A pantograph is a set of parallelogram links joined at pivots.

discovery.text: Moving one end traces the same path at the other end, scaled up or down.

twist.text: Train pantographs on rooftops use the same idea to reach overhead wires.

climax.text: Engravers once used pantographs to shrink designs onto coin dies.

punchline.text: A few bars can copy any shape at any size.

quiz.question: What does a pantograph mechanism do?
options: It converts rotary motion into linear motion
It reproduces motion at a scaled-up or scaled-down ratio
It locks a linkage at any position for precise holding
